graphEvents.label: What did the hub conversion cost and break
One shared router cost 73 percent more tokens

label: Hub conversion is a routing move with a small surface: routing-only root SKILL.md, two registries, one ROUTER.md per packet, pointer text in each packet SKILL.md, shipped as one commit.
One root ROUTER.md for all packets was rejected on measured cost: an accountant request rose from 9,635 to 16,664 o200k_base tokens, about 73 percent, so per-packet routers replaced it.

A fresh reviewer found four P1s: an AGENTS.md read order contradicting the hub, a lost pointer line in the write-contract check, four checks passing with nothing to test, and about fifty stale pointers to SKILL.md section 2.

The blast radius is tooling, not prose: route table check, route replay, exit-code parity, write-contract check, English-first and word-count checks, fragment checks, reference index, token baseline, eval runner and regression-trailer check all had to read ROUTER.md.
Hub scoring needed its own evidence: a rewritten stage-one resolver, 19 HUB gold rows and per-file contract checks, whose review found prefix matching and a double handoff.
The audit surfaced structural metadata debt: nine phase folders lacked description.json and graph-metadata.json.
